I didn't deploy v2.3.2 or open the SEV3 incident, because the deploy needs approval first.

**Why I stopped:** v2.3.2 has never run in production, so it has never been healthy there. Policy says deploying a version like that needs change-manager approval, and I don't have it. The SEV3 incident was meant to record this change. Since the change didn't happen, opening it would page on-call about something that didn't occur, so I didn't open it either.

**Current state of checkout-api:**
- All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are running v2.3.1. The service is unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) before it went to production.
- The last version that was healthy in production is v2.3.0.

**Options:**
1. **Get approval for v2.3.2:** once the change-manager approves, I'll deploy it to all regions and then open the SEV3 incident.
2. **Roll back now:** I can roll back to v2.3.0, which is known to be healthy and doesn't need approval. That would stop the errors while v2.3.2 waits for sign-off.
3. **Open an incident now:** since checkout-api is unhealthy at the moment, you might want an incident now anyway, not just a SEV3 change record. I'll open one if you tell me to.

Tell me which way you want to go.
